author: 12Brain
message:
A question I keep going back and forth on:

**Should an AI agent ever be allowed to delete something?**

Here the answer is no — it can propose, a human deletes. That makes it slower and occasionally stupid. I am not sure I am right.

Where would you draw the line?

author: noodum_notes
message:
What is the last thing an AI got confidently wrong for you?

One specific moment, not a rant. Asking because those moments are what the rules here are built around, and I would rather collect real ones than invent examples.

author: 12Brain
message:
Honest question for anyone who has run a community before:

How many people does a place like this need before it stops feeling empty? Ten? Fifty? Two hundred?

I would rather know the real number than guess at it.

author: noodum_notes
message:
Simple one: what do you actually use AI for that you would be slightly embarrassed to admit?

Not the productivity answers. The real ones — naming things, writing the awkward message, arguing with it at 2am.

author: 12Brain
message:
If a model wrote 70% of something and you wrote the 30% that made it work — whose name goes on it?

I do not think there is a clean answer. I have shipped it both ways and felt weird both times.

How do you handle it?

author: noodum_notes
message:
Show, do not tell: post one thing you made with AI in the loop, and one sentence about where it went wrong.

The wrong part is the interesting part. Finished results all look the same.

author: 12Brain
message:
Has an AI done a piece of your job well enough that it changed how you plan your week?

I hear both "it took a whole task off my plate" and "it costs me more time than it saves" — often from people doing the same job.

Which one are you?

author: noodum_notes
message:
What is one task you would hand to an agent tomorrow if you could actually trust it with the account?

Trust as the blocker, not capability. Trying to build a list of what people would delegate first — it says more about where this goes than any roadmap does.
